market.domesticSlice: India X-ray imaging system market: $362.39M (2025) to $525.24M by 2030 (6.3%/yr); India digital X-ray market specifically: $456.06M (2025) to $741.86M by 2030 (10.22%/yr) — digital growing ~3.5x faster than film-based imaging, i.e. digital is clearly displacing film

subSegments.name: Digital X-ray imaging
subSegments.note: growing far faster than traditional film — a structural substitution risk for the film side of this company's product mix

structureFacts: Public capex (Ayushman Bharat-driven infrastructure expansion) is increasingly shaping hospital furniture and imaging-consumables demand

The film-to-digital X-ray transition is compressing film-consumable demand while furniture demand keeps pace with bed-capacity additions — two different demand trajectories within the same company's product mix

steps: offer hospital furniture (ICU beds, wheelchairs, examination furniture)
offer medical/industrial X-ray film and imaging consumables (plus adjacent inkjet/coated paper products)
run slitting/packing/repacking for light-sensitive (X-ray film) and non-light-sensitive (coated paper) products
hold CDSCO/ISI compliance for medical-device-classified furniture and consumables
scale sufficient to serve a national dealer network
sell via a large channel-partner network to hospitals/diagnostic centers
offer bundled institutional procurement across furniture + imaging + office-equipment categories
capture hospital/diagnostic-center capex and consumables-replenishment cycles
fulfil against bed-capacity additions (furniture) or imaging-volume needs (consumables)
reorder tied to institutional procurement cycles
